source_text.body:
Upgrade vulnerable dependencies via automated pull request
Devin opened a PR on a Spring Boot and Next.js sample app upgrading dependencies to fix listed CVEs, including 103 npm vulnerabilities on the frontend.
·
Apr 29, 2026
Done with
DE
Devin
What they did
Requested by a user in a Devin session, Devin audited the Spring Boot backend and Next.js frontend and pushed two commits. These upgraded Spring Boot, sqlite-jdbc, Gradle, Next.js, React, axios and marked. It also fixed plaintext password storage, a hardcoded JWT secret and wildcard CORS, and adapted code to SWR v2 and React 18. It left a human checklist for manual testing.
How it went
Frontend npm vulnerabilities fell from 103 (10 critical) to 2 (0 critical). The PR was closed unmerged, superseded by #366. Devin's own review flagged an XSS regression: the marked sanitize option was dropped with no replacement.
Worth knowing
Library upgrades can silently drop safety options such as marked's sanitize. Check for that, and set JWT_SECRET before deploying. The PR also notes JaCoCo coverage failed at 33%, a pre-existing condition.
Try it yourself
with
Devin
Copy prompt
In my repo [repo URL], upgrade the vulnerable dependencies in [frontend/backend/both] to fix the known CVEs reported by [npm audit / Dependabot / scanner name]. Make sure the build and existing tests still pass after the upgrades. Open a pull request listing which vulnerabilities were fixed, which remain, and any breaking changes you had to handle. Don't merge it.
Original source: https://github.com/Cognition-Partner-Workshops/uc-cve-remediation-regulatory-compliance/pull/181
